title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Nd3+ and Ho3+ are underused for luminescent SMMs: Nd3+ barriers stay small because low axiality is hard to impose on early lanthanides, and Ho3+ suffers strong QTM from its non-Kramers character and I = 7/2 hyperfine coupling, with no luminescent Ho3+ SMM known to the authors.
explanation: The only Nd magneto-optical comparison cited is the homoleptic tris(pyrazolyl)borate SMM set against an earlier optical-absorption crystal-field study. For Ho3+, combined crystal-field and hyperfine effects can suppress zero-field QTM, so the ion is still considered promising. A few Ce3+ SMMs exist, but their luminescence was not studied; Ce3+ emission is a broad allowed 4f–5d transition rather than a narrow 4f–4f line.
scope: Nd3+, Ho3+, and Ce3+ molecular magnets considered as potential luminescent SMMs.
caveats: Absence of Ho3+ luminescent SMMs is the authors’ knowledge claim at the time of the review, not a physical prohibition.
